To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the cranking model is a special case of the HFB-projected model, 2) the HFB-projector provides a new and very efficient tool for the description of the rotational motion of nuclei, 3) the HFB-projection model is the most accurate method to describe nuclear rotation in the framework of the HFB-theory.
(1) The projected HFB-equations are solved for the first time in a systematic way.
the projected HFB-Theory can be applied to collective nuclear rotations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a microscopic model for nuclear collective motion.
the following topics: 1) Theoretical investigations of the collective rotation of nuclei in the HFB-framework.
the development and application of the projected HFB-Theory to the description of collective nuclear rotation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HFB-theory with the projection method provides a consistent and powerful tool to describe collective nuclear rotation.
the HFB-Theory, in the form presented here, is not capable to describe collective nuclear rotation.
the HFB-Theory in its cranking model version is an excellent approximation of the projected HFB-Equation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “projected HFB-Equation” is equivalent to the cranking equation.
a cranking solution is obtained from the projected HFB-equations.
the HFB-Theory with projection is the most general and consistent theory for the description of the rotational motion of nuclei.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the projected energy can be expressed as a sum of two parts, one of which can be identified with a cranking energy and the other one with the HFB energy of the corresponding non-rotating system.
the cranking-model is not an approximate model for the rotational states but the exact solution of the HFB-Equation.
the projected HFB-Energy is a functional of the density matrix and can be minimized in a self-consistent way.
